questions.stem: Which short phrase is used to describe Data Tokenisation in relation to Data Masking?
options: Data Masking without a key
Data Masking for unstructured data
Data Masking with Mappability
Data Masking in real time
Data Masking by summarisation
questions.explanation: Data Tokenisation is described as Data Masking with Mappability, because the mapping back to the original data is preserved.

questions.stem: In Data Tokenisation, what replaces the sensitive data in the actual data store?
options: A unique system-generated value called a Token
A random value with no record kept
A summarised range
A hashed password
A blank field
questions.explanation: Data Tokenisation replaces sensitive data with a unique system-generated value called a Token.

questions.stem: Where are the original data, the token and their mapping details kept in Data Tokenisation?
options: In the same table as the token
In the application log
In the user's browser
They are discarded once the token is issued
In a Token Vault stored externally for safe keeping
questions.explanation: During tokenisation the original data plus the token and mapping details are stored in a Token Vault somewhere external.

questions.stem: What is the major difference between Data Tokenisation and Data Masking?
options: Tokenisation works only on numbers, masking on text
Tokenised data is always reversible, whereas masked data is no longer reversible once changed
Masking requires a vault, tokenisation does not
Tokenisation is done manually, masking automatically
Masking is used for privacy, tokenisation for performance
questions.explanation: Because the mapping stays safe in the Token Vault, tokenised data is always reversible, in contrast with masking where randomly changed data cannot be recovered.

questions.stem: Which Data Warehousing concept is offered as a quick analogy for Data Tokenisation?
options: Fact table
Slowly changing dimension
Star schema
Surrogate Key
Materialised view
questions.explanation: A Surrogate Key replaces original business keys with unique auto-generated values while the original data is not touched, much like a token.

questions.stem: How does the location of a Surrogate Key in Data Warehousing differ from the location of the equivalent key in Data Tokenisation?
options: Both reside in the Token Vault
In Data Warehousing it resides with the actual data, whereas in Data Tokenisation it resides in the Token Vault
In Data Warehousing it resides in the Token Vault, whereas in Data Tokenisation it resides with the actual data
Both reside with the actual data
Neither is stored anywhere
questions.explanation: In Data Warehousing the Surrogate Key resides along with the actual data, whereas in Data Tokenisation the equivalent key resides in the Token Vault.

questions.stem: What does Data Masking do to sensitive data?
options: Stores it in an external vault
Keeps a mapping so it can be restored
Replaces it with an auto-generated business key
Changes it to random values so that an individual cannot be identified if the data reaches the wrong hands
Encrypts it with a recoverable key
questions.explanation: Data Masking changes data with random values to hide the original, so nobody can identify the individual the record refers to.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about Data Tokenisation is NOT correct?
options: The original data is destroyed once the token is issued
The token replaces the original data in the actual data store
The mapping between token and original is kept in a Token Vault
The actual data is always reversible
It is often mixed up with Data Masking
questions.explanation: The original data is not destroyed; it is stored with the token and mapping details in the Token Vault.

questions.stem: Why is masked data no longer reversible?
options: Because the vault is deleted after masking
Because masking is applied only in transit
Because masked data is compressed
Because regulators forbid reversing it
Because the sensitive data has been randomly changed with no mapping retained
questions.explanation: After sensitive data is randomly changed by masking there is no mapping back, so it is no longer reversible.

questions.stem: In Data Tokenisation, what role does the token play in the actual data store?
options: It is stored alongside the original value as a duplicate
It encrypts the original value in place
It replaces the original data while the mapping stays safe in the Token Vault
It flags the record for deletion
It is only used in reports
questions.explanation: The token replaces the original data in the actual data store, and its mapping details remain safe in the Token Vault.
